$comment: CANONICAL SUBSYSTEM PATH TAXONOMY. Owned by CRT (critic doctrine). This file is the single source of truth for the `judges:` values a reference item may claim and for the subsystem path a builder task may name. INDEX.md is GENERATED from this file + a scan of corpus/**/RI-*.md by tools/corpus-index.mjs. To add a path: append here (append-only; never renumber, never silently rename), then regenerate the index. A path that appears in an RI's `judges:` but not here is an ORPHAN and is reported by the generator. | WAVE 0 AUDIT (corpus-audit): 123 paths appended across eight new roots (weapon, magic, character, stealth, crime, experience, composition, journey, input) plus world.* and lore.* additions; 5 new critic roles. Every appended record carries a `registered` field naming its source. Shared NUMBERS are registered separately in corpus/00-doctrine/constants.json - subsystems.json owns paths, constants.json owns values.

arb_legend.souls: Inside the fight. Souls is authoritative (ARBITRATION.md §1).
arb_legend.morrowind: Outside the fight. Morrowind is authoritative (ARBITRATION.md §1).
arb_legend.modern-fidelity: Judged against current-generation graphics references ONLY (ARBITRATION.md §4).
arb_legend.art-direction: Judged against Morrowind / strangeness references ONLY (ARBITRATION.md §4).
arb_legend.split: A pre-decided seam. See the named seam ruling in ARBITRATION.md §2.
arb_legend.neutral: Neither side is authoritative; the corpus item defines the bar outright.

critics.critic.combat: Judges the fight. Must run the combat harness and read traces, never source.
critics.critic.progression: Judges levelling, economy, build identity, bonfires, equipment.
critics.critic.quests: Judges quest structure, faction escalation, resolution breadth.
critics.critic.dialogue: Judges topic graphs, disposition, rumours, NPC voice.
critics.critic.journal: Judges journal text as written, entry by entry.
critics.critic.world: Judges map, density, traversal, settlements, strangeness.
critics.critic.lore: Judges canon adherence, book structure, unreliable narration.
critics.critic.fidelity: Judges graphics quality against MODERN references only.
critics.critic.artdirection: Judges art direction against MORROWIND references only.
critics.critic.platform: Judges frame budget, load, input latency, persistence in a real browser.
critics.critic.coherence: End-of-wave whole-game agent. Fixes coherence, never quality. See COHERENCE-AGENT.md.
critics.critic.weapons: Judges weapon classes, movesets, contextual attacks and weapon feel. Must run the moveset validator over game/data/combat/movesets/** and read frame traces, never source. Requested by the weapons agent, wave 0.
critics.critic.magic: Judges the effect catalogue, spellmaking, enchanting and utility magic outside the fight. Must run the static analyser over game/data/magic/** and the quest analyser over game/data/quests/**, never source. magic.casting.* stays with critic.combat - it is inside the fight and AR-1 applies. Requested by the magic agent, wave 0.
critics.critic.journey: Judges END-TO-END PLAYER SEQUENCES rather than subsystems: first launch, the first hour, controls, save/load, death, a quest without markers, returning after a week. Scores the seams BETWEEN subsystems, which no subsystem critic owns. Requested by the journeys agent, wave 0.
critics.critic.experience: Judges the played experience and system composition: opening hook, anecdote census, session shape, novelty curve, endings, permissiveness, and the cross-system payoff matrix. Bound by PLAYTHROUGH-CRITIC.md section 4 - it may not report on fun directly. Requested by the experience agent, wave 0.
critics.critic.stealth: Judges detection, sneak, theft, lockpicking, trespass and fencing, plus the crime loop: witnesses, bounty, guard response, arrest, jail, and faction-sanctioned crime. Requested by this audit; the character/stealth/crime agent registered 28 paths with no critic.

aliases_note: RECONCILIATION LAYER. Reference items written before/alongside this taxonomy used their own path spellings. Each entry maps a legacy path to its canonical path so the index still resolves. Aliases are a MIGRATION AID, not a second vocabulary: tools/corpus-index.mjs lists every item still using a legacy spelling in INDEX.md section 4, and those items' front-matter should be corrected to the canonical path when next touched. NEW reference items MUST use canonical paths only.

judged_by_doctrine_note: Some subsystem paths are judged by a doctrine document rather than by a reference item. They are NOT corpus holes: the named document carries the bar, the method, and the evidence requirement. Everything else must have an RI.
